Programmable physical control devices are increasingly becoming central to advanced users' workflows, including agentic AI programming. Logitech is now officially launching a compact solution to market, suitable for any desktop environment.

Logitech today announced the MX Keypad, a $99.99 accessory featuring nine customizable full-color LCD keys that can be used to launch commands, execute macros, and open AI tools.

The MX Keypad is priced at half the cost of Logitech's MX Creative Console.

If the hardware looks familiar, here's the backstory. Logitech's MX Creative Console combines an LCD keypad with a separate dial controller, allowing users to adjust settings and operate creative applications.

The MX Keypad offers you the keypad experience, but without the need for that extra controller, priced at just half the $199.99 MSRP of the Creative Console.

The new product's main selling points are developers and AI workflows, but the customization features are not limited to coding applications.

Customize the experience through Logi Options+ software

Users can use the free Logi Options+ software to assign shortcuts, pre-saved prompt commands, scripts, and macros to individual keys. Two page buttons can store up to 15 pages, and app-aware profiles automatically switch layouts when users move between different apps.

This means the same set of physical buttons can perform different functions in VS Code, Slack, Chrome, or other apps. The Logi Marketplace offers plugins, profiles, and icon packs, while the built-in icon editor allows users to design the appearance of each key.

You can use AI to program your AI keypad

My initial hands-on test was connecting the MX Keypad to a MacBook Air on the desk, then asking Codex to use computer control features and, based on my ChatGPT usage habits on Mac, help me program custom keys, set up within Logi Options+.

Asking an AI coding agent to set up your physical control keys for AI work is rather interesting. At the same time, it clearly states its appeal: putting the prompt commands and actions you frequently click onto dedicated, labeled keys.

Logitech partnered with GitHub to develop the MX Keypad. The product features built-in GitHub Copilot integration for VS Code, and both new and existing users can claim a three-month free Copilot Pro+ subscription through Logi Options+.

MX Keypad supports community plugins

Logitech also stated that community plugins for Claude Code and OpenAI Codex offer agent status tracking, terminal control, and other features. Developers looking to go further can use the Logi Actions SDK, which supports C# and Node.js, to write their own plugins.

This keypad connects via USB-C and supports macOS 13 or above, as well as Windows 10 or above operating systems. It measures approximately 3.6 x 3.1 inches and weighs 96 grams, so it won't take up much space next to a laptop or keyboard.

The MX Keypad is officially on sale from today (September 8), available in Graphite and Pale Grey, priced at $99.99.
